questions.stemHtml: A 48-year-old female comes into the ER with chest pain. An electrocardiogram shows the following finding. The QR segment best correlates with which part of the action potential of the ventricular myocyte, as shown in Image B?

options.label: A
options.text: Phase 0, which is primarily characterized by sodium Influx.

options.label: B
options.text: Phase 0, which is primarily characterized by potassium efflux

options.label: C
options.text: Phase 1, which is primarily characterized by potassium and chloride efflux.

options.label: D
options.text: Phase 1, which is primarily characterized by calcium efflux.

questions.answerText: Phase 0, which is primarily characterized by sodium Influx.
questions.solutionHtml:
Phase 0, which is primarily characterized by sodium Influx.
  • The QR segment corresponds to ventricular depolarization, which is Phase 0 of the myocyte action potential and is characterized by sodium influx.
  • This coordinated action of ventricular myocytes is caused by the opening of the fast Na+ channels that allow an influx of Na+ ions into the cell in Phase 0 of the action potential, leading to rapid depolarization.
  • This portion of the action potential is affected by Class I antiarrhythmics, such as propafenone and flecainide.
  • Image A shows a labeled beat with a P wave, QRS complex, and T wave.
  • Image B shows a cardiac action potential with the phases labeled.


Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 128

questions.stem: An emergency room physician performs carotid massage in an attempt to slow the heart rate of a patient with supraventricular tachycardia. The physician explains to the patient that this maneuver is expected to increase vagal stimulation. A dramatic increase in the activity of vagal preganglionic axons is most likely to result in which of the following?

options.label: A
options.text: Decrease the RR interval

options.label: B
options.text: Decrease the number of QRS complexes relative to the number of P waves

options.label: C
options.text: Decrease the PR interval

options.label: D
options.text: Decrease the duration of the ST segment

questions.solutionHtml:
Decrease the RR interval

Dramatically increased release of acetylcholine (ACh) from post-ganglionic neurons, strongly excited by vagal preganglionic axons, will hyperpolarize AV nodal fibers sufficiently to block a fraction of the impulses being conducted through the AV node. This leads to partial (second-degree) or total (third-degree) heart block. The vagal activity also will decrease rather than increase heart rate.




Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 128

questions.stem: Jitendra, a 23-year-old medical student, is participating in a cardiac echocardiography study. During the isovolumetric ventricular contraction phase of the cardiac cycle, which of the following findings take place?

options.label: A
options.text: Aortic blood pressure is falling

options.label: B
options.text: Aortic Valve is open

options.label: C
options.text: AV valves open

options.label: D
options.text: Second heart sound is produced

questions.solutionHtml:
Aortic blood pressure is falling

During isovolumetric ventricular contraction, ventricular myocytes are depolarized and contract forcefully. Pressure within the ventricle is rising so that it is greater than atrial pressure but less than aortic pressure. Thus, both the AV and the aortic valves are closed. The first, not the second, heart sound is heard as the AV valve closes. Because blood is still flowing out of the aorta during this time, aortic pressure is falling.




Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 128-131

questions.stemHtml: Which of the provided images is correctly labeled for the electrode placement and polarity of the three standard limb leads?

options.label: A
options.text: A

options.label: B
options.text: B

options.label: C
options.text: C

options.label: D
options.text: D

questions.solutionHtml:
B
  • Standard limb lead I is between the right arm and the left arm (positive electrode on the left arm).
  • Standard limb lead II is between the right arm and the left leg (positive electrode on the left leg).
  • Standard limb lead III is between the left arm and the left leg (positive electrode on the left leg).
  • Bipolar limb leads (frontal plane):
  • Lead I: RA (-) to LA (+) (Right Left, or lateral)
  • Lead II: RA (-) to LL (+) (Superior Inferior)
  • Lead III: LA (-) to LL (+) (Superior Inferior)
  • Augmented unipolar limb leads (frontal plane):
  • Lead aVR: RA (+) to [LA & LL] (-) (Rightward)
  • Lead aVL: LA (+) to [RA & LL] (-) (Leftward)
  • Lead aVF: LL (+) to [RA & LA] (-) (Inferior)
  • Unipolar (+) chest leads (horizontal plane):
  • Leads V1, V2, V3: (Posterior Anterior)
  • Leads V4, V5, V6:(Right Left, or lateral)



Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 524,525

questions.stem: Stimulation of the parasympathetic nerves to the normal heart can lead to complete inhibition of the SA node for several seconds. During that period:

options.label: A
options.text: P waves would become larger.

options.label: B
options.text: There would be fewer T waves than QRS complexes.

options.label: C
options.text: There would be fewer P waves than T waves.

options.label: D
options.text: There would be fewer QRS complexes than P waves.

questions.answerText: There would be fewer P waves than T waves.
questions.solutionHtml:
There would be fewer P waves than T waves.

In the Parasympathetic condition, blood flows into the ventricles, and less muscle contraction is required here. This is why the P wave is smaller than the T wave.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 524-526.Guyton and Hall, Textbook of Medical Physiology, 14th Edition, Page Number: 134-137.

questions.stem: The P wave is normally positive in lead I of the ECG because ——

options.label: A
options.text: Depolarization of the ventricles proceeds from the subendocardium to the Sub epicardium.

options.label: B
options.text: When the ECG electrode attached to the right arm is positive relative to the electrode attached to the left arm, an upward deflection is recorded.

options.label: C
options.text: AV nodal conduction is slower than atrial conduction.

options.label: D
options.text: Depolarization of the atria proceeds from right to left.

questions.answerText: Depolarization of the atria proceeds from right to left.
questions.solutionHtml:
Depolarization of the atria proceeds from right to left.

The normal P wave reflects these activation patterns. Thus, P waves are positive in lead II and usually in leads I, aVL, and aVF, reflecting the leftward and inferior direction of activation during sinus rhythm.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 524,525.

questions.stem: During the cardiac cycle, the correct statement is_______

options.label: A
options.text: The aortic and mitral valves are never open at the same time.

options.label: B
options.text: The first heart sound is caused by the rapid ejection of blood from the ventricles.

options.label: C
options.text: The mitral valve is open throughout the diastole.

options.label: D
options.text: Left ventricular pressure is always less than aortic pressure.

questions.answerText: The aortic and mitral valves are never open at the same time.
questions.solutionHtml:
The aortic and mitral valves are never open at the same time.

The aortic and mitral valves are never open at the same time- During expiration, the pulmonary and aortic valves close at the same time; but during inspiration, the aortic valve closes slightly before the pulmonary. The slower closure of the pulmonary valve is due to the lower impedance of the pulmonary vascular tree. They never open at the same time.




Ganong's Review of Medical Physiology, 26th Edition, Page Number: 509-510,
